newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Pakistani government sacks some civil servants.
newsitem.headline: New Pakistani government sacks some civil servants.

text.p: Pakistan's new caretaker government, in its first public action, sacked civil servants who had been re-hired on contract after retirement, the official news agency APP said on Tuesday.
The Establishment Division told all government ministries and departments to end the contracts of re-employed "retired civil servants" and to report back on implementation, APP said.
The decision appeared likely to mean that several senior civil servants whose careers had been extended by the ousted government of Benazir Bhutto would lose their jobs.
Earlier in the day, caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid told reporters that cutting non-development government spending would be high on his administration's agenda.
"Our top-most priority will be to cut expenditure and bring austerity," Khalid said. "We want to adopt true austerity, simplicity and cut down on wasteful expenditure."
President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's three-year government, dissolved parliament and called fresh elections for February 3 to be supervised by the caretaker government.
